children: shares climbed 4% in early trading Wednesday after the company secured a $1.2 billion order for AMD's Helios AI systems from cloud infrastructure provider Vultr.

The deal covers rack-scale systems combining 72 AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs with EPYC processors, Pensando networking hardware and ROCm software. HPE will also provide networking and liquid-cooling technology as part of the deployment.

The contract adds to HPE's AI infrastructure operations as cloud providers expand computing capacity for artificial intelligence workloads. AMD has positioned Helios as an integrated system combining chips, networking and software for large AI deployments.

HPE also raised its fiscal 2027 networking growth forecast to the high-teens to low-20s on a percentage basis. Data center networking revenue is expected to grow at a low-to-high 50s percentage compound annual rate through fiscal 2029, while routing revenue is projected to expand in the low-to-high 20s range.
Separately, HPE lifted its expected annual run-rate savings from the Juniper Networks acquisition to $800 million by the end of fiscal 2028.

title: HPE Shares Jump on $1.2 Billion AMD AI Deal
